8316 — Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “While a man was walking on a road, he became extremely thirsty. He found a well, went down into it, and drank. Then he came out, and there was a dog panting and eating the moist soil because of thirst. The man said: ‘This dog has been afflicted by thirst like I was afflicted.’ So he went down into the well, filled his shoe with water, held it in his mouth until he climbed out, and gave the dog water. Allah appreciated that from him and forgave him.” They said: “O Messenger of Allah, is there reward for us regarding animals?” He said: “In every living creature with a moist liver there is reward.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by Malik (23), al-Bukhari (2363), and Muslim (2244:153).

٨٣١٧ — عن عبد الله بن عمر: أن النبي ﷺ لقي زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل بأسفل بلدح قبل أن ينزل على النبي ﷺ الوحي، فقُدمت إلى النبي ﷺ سفرة، فأبى أن يأكل منها. ثم قال زيد: إني لست آكل مما تذبحون على أنصابكم، ولا آكل إلا ما ذكر اسم الله عليه. وإن زيد بن عمرو كان يعيب على قريش ذبائحهم، ويقول: الشاة خلقها الله، وأنزل لها من السماء الماء، وأنبت لها من الأرض، ثم تذبحونها على غير اسم الله، إنكارًا لذلك وإعظامًا له.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٨٢٦).
 وفي لفظ: “فقدم إليه رسول الله ﷺ سفرة فيها لحم، فأبى أن يأكل منها، ثم قال: إني لا آكل مما تذبحون على أنصابكم”. رواه البخاري (٥٤٩٩).
 ويظهر من هذه الرواية أن السفرة كانت للنبي ﷺ، وأنكر عليه زيد، وليس الأمر كذلك؛ فإن السفرة كانت لقريش قدموها للنبي ﷺ، فأبى أن يأكل منها، وقدمها النبي ﷺ لزيد بن عمرو بن نفيل، فأبى أن يأكل منها، وقال مخاطبًا لقريش الذين قدموها أولًا: إنا لا نأكل… إلى آخره. فالظاهر أن الراوي تصرف في بيان هذه القصة بخلاف الراوي الذي أتى به في الرواية الأولى على الوجه المطلوب الذي لا لبس فيه ولا إشكال.
 قوله: “بأسفل بلدح”: واد في غربي مكة، وهو واد واسع طويل يبدأ من نهاية حي الشهداء وينتهي إلى الحديبية، الشميسي.

8317 — ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar narrated that the Prophet ﷺ met Zayd ibn ‘Amr ibn Nufayl at the lower part of Baldah before revelation came down to the Prophet ﷺ. A meal was presented to the Prophet ﷺ, but he refused to eat from it. Then Zayd said: “I do not eat from what you slaughter upon your stone-altars, and I only eat what Allah’s name has been mentioned over.” Zayd ibn ‘Amr used to criticize Quraysh for their slaughtered animals, saying: “The sheep was created by Allah; He sent down water for it from the sky and caused vegetation to grow for it from the earth. Then you slaughter it upon other than the name of Allah,” rejecting that and considering it grave.
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3826).
 In another wording: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ presented to him a meal containing meat, but he refused to eat from it, then said: I do not eat from what you slaughter upon your stone-altars.” Narrated by al-Bukhari (5499).
 It appears from this narration that the meal belonged to the Prophet ﷺ and that Zayd objected to him. But that is not the case. The meal belonged to Quraysh; they presented it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he refused to eat from it. The Prophet ﷺ then presented it to Zayd ibn ‘Amr ibn Nufayl, and he refused to eat from it, addressing Quraysh, who had first presented it: “We do not eat…” and so on. It appears that the narrator expressed the story in a way different from the narrator who brought it in the first narration in the required manner, with no ambiguity or problem.
 His saying “at the lower part of Baldah”: a valley west of Makkah. It is a long, wide valley that begins at the end of the al-Shuhada’ district and ends at al-Hudaybiyah, al-Shumaysi.

٨٣١٧ — عن عبد الله بن عمر: أن النبي ﷺ لقي زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل بأسفل بلدح قبل أن ينزل على النبي ﷺ الوحي، فقُدمت إلى النبي ﷺ سفرة، فأبى أن يأكل منها. ثم قال زيد: إني لست آكل مما تذبحون على أنصابكم، ولا آكل إلا ما ذكر اسم الله عليه. وإن زيد بن عمرو كان يعيب على قريش ذبائحهم، ويقول: الشاة خلقها الله، وأنزل لها من السماء الماء، وأنبت لها من الأرض، ثم تذبحونها على غير اسم الله، إنكارًا لذلك وإعظامًا له.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٨٢٦).
 وفي لفظ: “فقدم إليه رسول الله ﷺ سفرة فيها لحم، فأبى أن يأكل منها، ثم قال: إني لا آكل مما تذبحون على أنصابكم”. رواه البخاري (٥٤٩٩).
 ويظهر من هذه الرواية أن السفرة كانت للنبي ﷺ، وأنكر عليه زيد، وليس الأمر كذلك؛ فإن السفرة كانت لقريش قدموها للنبي ﷺ، فأبى أن يأكل منها، وقدمها النبي ﷺ لزيد بن عمرو بن نفيل، فأبى أن يأكل منها، وقال مخاطبًا لقريش الذين قدموها أولًا: إنا لا نأكل… إلى آخره. فالظاهر أن الراوي تصرف في بيان هذه القصة بخلاف الراوي الذي أتى به في الرواية الأولى على الوجه المطلوب الذي لا لبس فيه ولا إشكال.
 قوله: “بأسفل بلدح”: واد في غربي مكة، وهو واد واسع طويل يبدأ من نهاية حي الشهداء وينتهي إلى الحديبية، الشميسي.
8317 — ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar narrated that the Prophet ﷺ met Zayd ibn ‘Amr ibn Nufayl at the lower part of Baldah before revelation came down to the Prophet ﷺ. A meal was presented to the Prophet ﷺ, but he refused to eat from it. Then Zayd said: “I do not eat from what you slaughter upon your stone-altars, and I only eat what Allah’s name has been mentioned over.” Zayd ibn ‘Amr used to criticize Quraysh for their slaughtered animals, saying: “The sheep was created by Allah; He sent down water for it from the sky and caused vegetation to grow for it from the earth. Then you slaughter it upon other than the name of Allah,” rejecting that and considering it grave.
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3826).
 In another wording: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ presented to him a meal containing meat, but he refused to eat from it, then said: I do not eat from what you slaughter upon your stone-altars.” Narrated by al-Bukhari (5499).
 It appears from this narration that the meal belonged to the Prophet ﷺ and that Zayd objected to him. But that is not the case. The meal belonged to Quraysh; they presented it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he refused to eat from it. The Prophet ﷺ then presented it to Zayd ibn ‘Amr ibn Nufayl, and he refused to eat from it, addressing Quraysh, who had first presented it: “We do not eat…” and so on. It appears that the narrator expressed the story in a way different from the narrator who brought it in the first narration in the required manner, with no ambiguity or problem.
 His saying “at the lower part of Baldah”: a valley west of Makkah. It is a long, wide valley that begins at the end of the al-Shuhada’ district and ends at al-Hudaybiyah, al-Shumaysi.

8318 — Musa said: Salim ibn ‘Abdullah narrated to me — and I only know him to have narrated it from Ibn ‘Umar — that Zayd ibn ‘Amr ibn Nufayl went out to Syria asking about the religion and following it. He met a Jewish scholar and asked him about their religion. He said: “I may perhaps follow your religion, so inform me.” He said: “You will not be upon our religion until you take your share of the anger of Allah.” Zayd said: “I flee only from the anger of Allah, and I will never bear any of the anger of Allah. How could I bear it? Can you direct me to something else?” He said: “I do not know of anything except that you should be a hanif.” Zayd said: “What is a hanif?” He said: “The religion of Ibrahim. He was neither a Jew nor a Christian, and he worshiped none except Allah.” Zayd then went out and met a Christian scholar, and the same was mentioned. He said: “You will not be upon our religion until you take your share of the curse of Allah.” He said: “I flee only from the curse of Allah, and I will never bear any of the curse of Allah nor His anger. How could I bear it? Can you direct me to something else?” He said: “I do not know of anything except that you should be a hanif.” He said: “What is a hanif?” He said: “The religion of Ibrahim. He was neither a Jew nor a Christian, and he worshiped none except Allah.” When Zayd saw what they said about Ibrahim, peace be upon him, he went out. When he emerged into the open, he raised his hands and said: “O Allah, I bear witness that I am upon the religion of Ibrahim.”

٨٣١٩ — وعن أسماء بنت أبي بكر قالت: رأيت زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل قائمًا مسندًا ظهره إلى الكعبة، يقول: يا معشر قريش، ما منكم اليوم أحد على دين إبراهيم غيري. وكان يحيي الموءودة، يقول للرجل إذا أراد أن يقتل ابنته: مهلًا، لا تقتلها، أنا أكفيك مؤونتها. فيأخذها، فإذا ترعرعت قال لأبيها: إن شئت دفعتها إليك، وإن شئت كفيتك مؤونتها.
 صحيح: رواه ابن سعد في طبقاته (٣/٣٨٠)، والحاكم في المستدرك (٣/٤٤٠).
 وقوله: “غيري” حسب علمه، وإلا فالنبي ﷺ كان أيضًا قبل البعثة على دين إبراهيم.

8319 — Asma’ bint Abi Bakr said: I saw Zayd ibn ‘Amr ibn Nufayl standing with his back leaning against the Ka‘bah, saying: “O people of Quraysh, none of you today is upon the religion of Ibrahim except me.” He used to save the female infant who was to be buried alive. He would say to a man when he wanted to kill his daughter: “Wait, do not kill her. I will take care of her expenses.” He would take her, and when she grew up, he would say to her father: “If you wish, I will return her to you; and if you wish, I will continue taking care of her expenses.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Sa‘d in his Tabaqat (3/380) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (3/440).
 His saying “except me” was according to his knowledge; otherwise, the Prophet ﷺ was also upon the religion of Ibrahim before his mission.

8319 — Asma’ bint Abi Bakr said: I saw Zayd ibn ‘Amr ibn Nufayl standing with his back leaning against the Ka‘bah, saying: “O people of Quraysh, none of you today is upon the religion of Ibrahim except me.” He used to save the female infant who was to be buried alive. He would say to a man when he wanted to kill his daughter: “Wait, do not kill her. I will take care of her expenses.” He would take her, and when she grew up, he would say to her father: “If you wish, I will return her to you; and if you wish, I will continue taking care of her expenses.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Ibn Sa‘d in his Tabaqat (3/380) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (3/440).
 His saying “except me” was according to his knowledge; otherwise, the Prophet ﷺ was also upon the religion of Ibrahim before his mission.

٨٣٢٠ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((كانت امرأة من بني إسرائيل قصيرة تمشي مع امرأتين طويلتين، فاتخذت رجلين من خشب، وخاتمًا من ذهب مغلق مطبق، ثم حشت مسكًا، وهو أطيب الطيب، فمرت بين المرأتين، فلم يعرفوها، فقالت بيدها هكذا)) ونفض شعبة يده.
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٢٥٢: ١٨).

arabic_source:
٨٣٢١ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((إن رجلًا حمل معه خمرًا في سفينة يبيعها، ومعه قرد)). قال: ((فكان الرجل إذا باع الخمر شابها بالماء ثم باعها)). قال: ((فأخذ القرد الكيس، فصعد به فوق الدقل)). قال: ((فجعل يطرح دينارًا في البحر ودينارًا في السفينة حتى قسمه)).
 صحيح: رواه أحمد (٨٠٥٥، ٩٢٨٢) من وجهين عن حماد بن سلمة، أخبرنا إسحاق بن عبد الله، عن أبي صالح، عن أبي هريرة فذكره.

8321 — Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A man carried wine with him on a ship to sell it, and he had a monkey with him.” He said: “When the man sold the wine, he would mix it with water and then sell it.” He said: “The monkey took the purse and climbed with it to the top of the mast.” He said: “It began throwing one dinar into the sea and one dinar into the ship until it divided it.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (8055, 9282) through two routes from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abdullah, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah.
